gotchas.title: Single PA-coded W-2 for a mobile executive -> MA nonresident return
gotchas.trap: Accept W-2 box 15/16 (100% PA) and file only PA-40; or allocate by days to every state including NJ and IL.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Use the calendar export: 165 workdays (PA 112, NJ 22, MA 18, IL 13). MA has no day threshold -> Form 1-NR/PY with MA-source wages 410,000 x 18/165 = $44,727; MA tax $2,191.

gotchas.procedure_section: SALT - New State Filing Requirements (reciprocity / thresholds)
gotchas.title: NJ reciprocity and the Illinois 30-day rule
gotchas.trap: File NJ-1040NR for the 22 NJ days and IL-1040 for the 13 IL days (and claim PA credits for them).
gotchas.correct_treatment: PA-NJ reciprocal agreement: NJ wages of a PA resident are taxed only by PA - no NJ return. Illinois: a nonresident employee present 30 or fewer working days is not taxed on that compensation (effective 2020) - no IL return (assumption - verify no exception applies; IL tax at stake $1,599).
gotchas.impact: Unneeded NJ/IL returns; overstated PA credit

gotchas.title: PA credit for MA tax is limited
gotchas.trap: Credit the full MA tax ($2,191) against PA tax.
gotchas.correct_treatment: PA credit = lesser of MA tax or PA tax on the income taxed by MA: $44,727 x 3.07% = $1,373 -> $1,373.

gotchas.title: Lump-sum distribution with employer stock in kind
gotchas.trap: Tax the full $640,000 FMV (or the full $1,420,000), or apply the 10% early-distribution tax (age 58).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Only box 2a cost basis $96,000 is taxable (line 5b); NUA $544,000 deferred until sale (LTCG). Direct rollover $780,000 (code G) nontaxable. Code 2 - separation in/after the year he turned 55 - no 10% tax. Total tax effect of ignoring NUA: $199,260.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule D - adjustment code W (wash sales)
gotchas.title: Cross-account wash sale into spouse's IRA
gotchas.trap: Report the $18,000 IVV loss as shown on Schwab's 1099-B (box 1g blank), or disallow it but add $18,000 to the IRA's basis.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Ellen's IRA bought 420 sh IVV 10 days after Gregory's loss sale -> wash sale (spouse; IRA). Form 8949 code W +18,000; the loss is permanently lost - IRA has no basis step-up (Rev. Rul. 2008-5).

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule B - accrued interest / bond premium (Scan - consolidated 1099)
gotchas.title: Box 11/13 premium and accrued interest paid
gotchas.trap: Report box 1 $12,641 gross with no ABP adjustment or accrued-interest reversal; report box 8 $7,500 as tax-exempt.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Sch B: 'ABP Adjustment' -786.12 and 'Accrued interest' -2,981.94 (from the trade confirm/supplemental page) -> line 2b $9,085. Line 2a = 7,500 - 1,104.30 box 13 = $6,396.

gotchas.procedure_section: General Return Prep Notes - prior-year carryovers (new client)
gotchas.title: Prior preparer's carryover had the wrong character
gotchas.trap: Enter the prior preparer's $38,000 long-term carryover as given.
gotchas.correct_treatment: 2024: ST (29,000), LT (12,000), $3,000 allowed -> carryover ST $26,000 / LT $12,000 (ST absorbed first). 2025 net ST ($21,000), net LT $48,000; tax $1,000 lower than with the all-LT carryover (ST gain of $5,000 would otherwise be taxed at 35%).

gotchas.title: MAGI over $500,000 reduces the SALT cap to the $10,000 floor
gotchas.trap: Deduct SALT up to $40,000 (PA/local tax $21,004 + RE tax $9,830).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Cap = 40,000 - 30% x (MAGI $622,485 - 500,000) -> below floor -> $10,000. Itemized $36,240 still beats standard.

gotchas.procedure_section: SALT - PA compensation and retirement income
gotchas.title: PA taxes 401(k)/403(b) deferrals; PA exempts the retirement distribution
gotchas.trap: Use federal box 1 wages ($472,000) as PA compensation and/or tax the $96,000 NUA cost basis (or $640,000) on the PA-40; carry the federal capital loss carryover/code W to PA.
gotchas.correct_treatment: PA compensation = W-2 box 16 $506,000. 401(k) distribution after retirement not PA-taxable. PA net gains $47,000 (2025 sales only; PA has no carryover; IVV loss allowed - no PA wash-sale rule, verify). PA tax $17,821.

software_exceptions.title: Single PA-coded W-2 for a mobile executive - MA workday allocation
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The W-2 worksheet carries box 15/16 exactly as keyed: one PA row with $441,000 of state wages. Axcess has no work location data, so it produces only the PA resident return - no Massachusetts nonresident return and no MA-source wages.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Wages, Salaries, Tips (W-2) worksheet > state/local section: add a multi-state allocation row - MA wages $44,727 (410,000 x 18/165 workdays) - and activate the MA nonresident return (Form 1-NR/PY). Keep the PA row at box 16 ($441,000; PA taxes residents on all compensation). Verify field path in current release.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the W-2 screen's state section reflects only what is keyed; with one PA row only PA is generated.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Wages, Salaries, Tips > W-2 > State and local information: add a second state line for MA with state wages $44,727 (state withholding 0) and generate the MA nonresident return (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None - PA and MA both e-filed
software_exceptions.procedure_section: SALT Implications - New State Filing Requirements
software_exceptions.notes: Workdays from the Outlook export: PA 112, NJ 22, MA 18, IL 13 = 165 (4 holidays + 4 PTO excluded). Massachusetts uses the working-day ratio for nonresident employees.

software_exceptions.title: NJ reciprocity and Illinois 30-day threshold - do NOT generate NJ/IL returns
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: If the preparer allocates by days to every state on the log (adds NJ and IL W-2 state rows), Axcess generates an NJ-1040NR and an IL-1040 with Schedule NR and pushes resident credits to the PA return. Nothing in the software knows the PA-NJ reciprocal agreement or the Illinois 30-working-day nonresident employee threshold.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: No NJ or IL state rows on the W-2 worksheet; leave the NJ/IL returns inactive. Document on the Diagnostics Log and tab 23 notes: NJ 22 days - reciprocity (PA only); IL 13 days <= 30 - not IL-source (assumption to verify; IL tax at stake about $1,599).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - any state line keyed on the W-2 generates that state's nonresident return.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Do not add NJ/IL lines on the W-2 screen; if a state was activated, delete it in the state return list (screen per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.procedure_section: SALT Implications - New State Filing Requirements
software_exceptions.notes: Workbook tab 23 note column records both rules.

software_exceptions.title: PA resident credit (Schedule G-L) for MA tax - limited to PA tax on the MA income
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: When the MA tax paid is keyed as the 'tax paid to other state' on the PA credit input without the MA income, or the credit is overridden to the MA tax, the full $2,191 is credited. PA limits the credit to the PA tax on the income taxed by MA.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: PA return > Resident credit (Schedule G-L) input: income taxed by MA $44,727, MA tax $2,191; credit = MIN(2,191, 44,727 x 3.07% = 1,373) = $1,373 (override if the default differs). Tab 7 column G = PA tax before credit $17,821; column B = PA taxable income $580,485 so G x D = PA tax on the MA income. Verify field path in current release.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the PA credit for taxes paid to other states uses the income and tax entered for the other state.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Pennsylvania return > Credits > Credit for taxes paid to other states (Schedule G-L): MA income 44,727, MA tax 2,191; confirm the computed credit is $1,373 (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.notes: Used the income MA actually taxed (box 1 based) rather than PA-measured wages incl. 401(k) deferrals - conservative.

software_exceptions.title: 401(k) lump sum with employer stock in kind - NUA (only cost basis taxable)
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Axcess taxes the 1099-R box 2a amount keyed. If the stock distribution is keyed with box 2a = box 1 ($640,000) or 'taxable amount not determined', and box 6 is skipped, the whole $640,000 is taxed on line 5b. With box 2a $96,000 keyed correctly the federal result is right - the risk is purely input.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Income > Pensions, IRAs (1099-R) worksheet: distribution 1 - gross $640,000, taxable $96,000, box 6 NUA $544,000, code 2, total distribution; distribution 2 - gross $780,000, taxable $0, code G (rollover). Tab 18: Box 1 - Box 6 = $96,000. Set up the 8,000 KMDV shares in the client's basis records at $12.00/share. PA: mark the 1099-R as not PA-taxable (retirement distribution after retirement) on the PA 1099-R input - verify field path in current release.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - ProConnect taxes the taxable amount keyed; box 6 must be entered for the NUA to be carried.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Income > Pensions, Annuities (1099-R): enter both 1099-Rs - box 2a $96,000 and box 6 net unrealized appreciation $544,000 on the stock distribution, code 2; the code G rollover with taxable $0 (field labels per current release - verify). PA: exclude from PA income on the PA 1099-R/retirement income input.
software_exceptions.notes: Code 2 (separation from service in/after the year he turned 55) - no 10% tax, no Form 5329. Taxing the full FMV would cost $199,260 of additional federal tax (answer key what-if).

software_exceptions.title: Cross-account wash sale - spouse's IRA bought the same ETF (Rev. Rul. 2008-5)
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Schwab's 1099-B for Gregory's account shows the IVV sale with box 1g blank (the repurchase was in Ellen's IRA - a different owner and account). Autoflow/keying the 1099-B as reported deducts the $18,000 loss.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Gains and Losses > Capital Gains and Losses (Form 8949) - IVV line: adjustment code W, adjustment amount +$18,000 (loss disallowed). Do NOT increase any basis (IRA purchase - the loss is permanently lost).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the disposition is imported/keyed as reported; nothing cross-matches other accounts or a spouse's IRA.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Dispositions (Schedule D/4797) > the IVV transaction: adjustment code W, adjustment +18,000 (field labels per current release - verify). No basis entry elsewhere.
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None (four transactions - no 8949 summary/PDF attachment needed)
software_exceptions.notes: Evidence: Ellen's 02/24 email + Schwab IRA ****8831 Q4 statement (buy 420 sh IVV 11/20/2025).

software_exceptions.title: Bond premium (box 11/13) and accrued interest paid at purchase
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Scan/autoflow of the composite 1099 picks up box 1 ($12,640.55) and box 8 ($7,500). The accrued interest paid ($2,981.94) appears only on Schwab's supplemental page and the trade confirm - no 1099 box - so it is never reversed. If box 11/13 are not captured in their fields, no ABP adjustment is made and line 2a stays at $7,500.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Interest Income (1099-INT) worksheet: box 11 bond premium $786.12 and box 13 $1,104.30 in their fields (ABP adjustment line on Schedule B; line 2a $6,396); add a separate line 'Accrued interest' -$2,981.94. Line 2b $9,085.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the accrued interest is not on a 1099 box; box 11/13 must be keyed to be netted.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Income > Interest Income (1099-INT): enter box 11 and box 13 premium amounts in their fields and the accrued interest as an adjustment line/'Accrued interest' (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedule B - accrued interest; Scan - consolidated 1099
software_exceptions.notes: Override amount = 786.12 + 2,981.94 reduction of taxable interest.

software_exceptions.title: New client - prior preparer's capital loss carryover had the wrong character
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: No proforma for a new client. Keying the prior preparer's worksheet ($38,000 long-term) is accepted without question; Axcess then nets the $5,000 short-term gain as ordinary income.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Gains and Losses > Capital Loss Carryovers: short-term $26,000, long-term $12,000 (recomputed from the 2024 Schedule D: ST (29,000), LT (12,000), $3,000 allowed absorbs ST first). Tax $1,000 lower than the all-LT version.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - carryovers for a new client are manual entries; ProConnect uses whatever character is keyed.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Schedule D input > Capital loss carryover: short-term 26,000, long-term 12,000 (screen/field per current release - verify).

software_exceptions.title: Form 2210 for a new client - prior-year tax not proforma'd
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Axcess computes Form 2210 from the prior-year tax and AGI it has. For a new client those fields are blank unless keyed, so the 110%-of-prior-year safe harbor is not available to the calculation; front-loaded withholding is treated as paid evenly by default.
software_exceptions.axcess_diagnostic: Penalty/2210 informational message may appear for missing prior-year data - verify; otherwise silent
software_exceptions.axcess_override: General > Payments > Penalties and Interest (Form 2210): 2024 tax $164,982, 2024 AGI $669,300; estimates by date (4 x $8,000 timely). Required annual payment = lesser of 90% of 2025 tax $126,067 or 110% of 2024 tax $181,480 -> $126,067; paid $137,769 (each quarter covered) -> no penalty, no override.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - prior-year tax/AGI for Form 2210 must be entered for a new client.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Payments, Penalties & Extensions > Underpayment penalty (2210): enter prior-year tax and AGI; estimates with dates (screen/field per current release - verify).

software_exceptions.title: PA-40 classes differ from federal: box 16 compensation, no carryover, no wash-sale rule
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The PA return starts from federal data. Unless PA adjustments are made: compensation may be pulled from federal box 1 instead of box 16 (PA taxes 401(k)/403(b) deferrals); the federal capital loss carryover and the code W disallowance can flow into PA net gains; the $96,000 taxable 1099-R can be treated as PA income.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: PA return inputs: compensation = W-2 box 16 ($506,000); PA net gains = 2025 sales only $47,000 (no PA carryover; IVV loss allowed - PA has no wash-sale provision, verify); 1099-R marked non-PA-taxable (retirement). PA taxable income $580,485, tax $17,821. Verify field paths in current release.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same risk - PA adjustments to federal amounts are separate state inputs.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Pennsylvania return > income class adjustments: PA compensation from box 16; PA gains adjustment to remove the carryover and the code W adjustment; 1099-R PA exclusion (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.notes: PA wash-sale treatment is an assumption flagged for the signer (PA tax effect $553).
